A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 2D radar can provide more accurate altitude estimate than the 3D radar in most of cases, except for the cases with accurate elevation measurement ( $\sigma _e<1^{\circ } $) and low indirect path PD.
the 2D radar is more suitable for altitude estimation than the 3D radar when the indirect path PD is low and the elevation measurement error s.d. is large.

a 2-D radar with multipath detections has the potential to achieve better altitude estimate accuracy than a 3-D airborne radar, but this is only possible with accurate indirect path measurements and a reliable indirect path detection method.

the 2- D radar can achieve better performance than the 3- D radar when the elevation measurement error is relatively large.
